items.stem: Which of the following best describes "vector"?
options: A quantity with both magnitude (size) and direction, such as a displacement or a velocity
The vector r = r₀ + tv for an object starting at r₀ and moving with constant velocity v
The position vector of the midpoint M of AB is ½(a + b)
Adding corresponding components: (a over b) + (c over d) = (a + c over b + d); geometrically, joining the vectors nose to tail
items.answer: A quantity with both magnitude (size) and direction, such as a displacement or a velocity
items.markingKey: A. "vector" is a quantity with both magnitude (size) and direction, such as a displacement or a velocity.

items.stem: "|(3 over 4)| = 3 + 4 = 7." Explain the flaw in this statement.
items.answer: Use Pythagoras: √(9 + 16) = 5.
items.markingKey: Use Pythagoras: √(9 + 16) = 5. 1 mark for identifying the error, 1-2 marks for the correct explanation.

items.stem: With the help of a specific example, explain why the vectors (3 over 4) and (−3 over −4) have the same magnitude but are not equal.
items.answer: Both have length √(9 + 16) = 5, but they point in opposite directions; equal vectors need the same magnitude and direction. (A specific, correct example that illustrates this is required for full marks.)
items.markingKey: Award marks for: Both have length √(9 + 16) = 5, but they point in opposite directions; equal vectors need the same magnitude and direction. (A specific, correct example that illustrates this is required for full marks.) (3 marks: one for each linked point in the chain of reasoning; no marks for assertion without explanation.)

items.stem: A vector has magnitude 9 and makes an angle of 325° anticlockwise with the positive x-axis. Write it as a column vector with components to 3 s.f.
A = (−8, 6) and B = (−1, 8). Find the vector AB, its exact magnitude and its direction measured anticlockwise from the positive x-axis (to 1 d.p.).
items.markingKey: AB = B − A (M1) = (7 over 2) (A1); magnitude √(49 + 4) (A1); direction from tan⁻¹ with the correct quadrant (A1).

items.stem: A tourist in Lima walks 4 km west and then 4 km north. (a) Write the displacement as a column vector (east, north). (b) Find its magnitude. (c) Find the bearing of the final position from the start. (d) Compare the distance walked with the magnitude of the displacement.
items.answer: (a) (−4 over 4) (b) 4√2 ≈ 5.66 km (c) 315° (d) the distance walked (8 km) is longer than the displacement
items.markingKey: (a) (−4 over 4) (b) 4√2 ≈ 5.66 km (c) 315° (d) the distance walked (8 km) is longer than the displacement. Vector components (A1 A1); magnitude / direction (M1 A1); interpretation or generalisation (B/D: R1).

items.stem: Which term matches this description: "A vector of magnitude 1; i = (1 over 0) and j = (0 over 1) are the unit vectors along the axes"?
items.answer: unit vector
items.markingKey: A. This is the definition of unit vector.

items.stem: Briefly explain why the vectors (3 over 4) and (−3 over −4) have the same magnitude but are not equal.
items.answer: Both have length √(9 + 16) = 5, but they point in opposite directions; equal vectors need the same magnitude and direction.
items.markingKey: Award marks for: Both have length √(9 + 16) = 5, but they point in opposite directions; equal vectors need the same magnitude and direction. (2 marks: one for each linked point in the chain of reasoning; no marks for assertion without explanation.)

items.stem: Explain what the vector −(3 over 4) represents and how it relates to (3 over 4).
items.answer: −(3 over 4) = (−3 over −4): the same magnitude 5 but the opposite direction.
items.markingKey: Components (A1); opposite direction (R1).

items.stem: A car drives at 83 km/h. Explain whether this is a speed or a velocity, and what extra information would make it the other.
items.answer: 83 km/h has no direction, so it is a speed (scalar); adding a direction, e.g. "83 km/h due north", makes it a velocity.
items.markingKey: Classification (A1); direction needed (R1).

items.stem: Find a vector of magnitude 40 in the same direction as (8 over 6).
items.answer: (32 over 24)
items.markingKey: |v| = 10 (A1); unit vector v/|v| (M1); × 40 (A1).

items.stem: "The magnitude of (−5 over 12) is −13 because one component is negative." Explain the flaw in this statement.
items.answer: A magnitude is a length and is never negative: √(25 + 144) = 13.
items.markingKey: A magnitude is a length and is never negative: √(25 + 144) = 13. 1 mark for identifying the error, 1-2 marks for the correct explanation.

items.stem: A = (−3, −3) and B = (3, −2). Find the vector AB, its exact magnitude and its direction measured anticlockwise from the positive x-axis (to 1 d.p.).
items.markingKey: AB = B − A (M1) = (6 over 1) (A1); magnitude √(36 + 1) (A1); direction from tan⁻¹ with the correct quadrant (A1).

items.stem: Investigate the vectors (6 over 8) and (8 over −6). (a) Find their magnitudes. (b) Find the direction of each from the positive x-axis. (c) Describe how they are related. (d) Generalise for (a over b) and (b over −a).
items.answer: (a) both have magnitude 10 (b) (6 over 8) points at 53.1°, (8 over −6) at 323.1° (c) they are perpendicular (90° apart) (d) (a, b) and (b, −a) are always perpendicular with equal magnitude
items.markingKey: (a) both have magnitude 10 (b) (6 over 8) points at 53.1°, (8 over −6) at 323.1° (c) they are perpendicular (90° apart) (d) (a, b) and (b, −a) are always perpendicular with equal magnitude. Vector components (A1 A1); magnitude / direction (M1 A1); interpretation or generalisation (B/D: R1).

items.stem: A delivery drone in Nairobi flies 122 m on a bearing of 120°. (a) Find the eastward and northward components. (b) Write its displacement as a column vector. (c) Check your answer by finding the magnitude. (d) Write the vector for the return journey and its bearing.
items.answer: (a) east 106 m, north −61.0 m (b) (106 over −61.0) (c) check √(106² + −61.0²) ≈ 122 m (d) the opposite vector (−106 over 61.0), bearing 300°
items.markingKey: (a) east 106 m, north −61.0 m (b) (106 over −61.0) (c) check √(106² + −61.0²) ≈ 122 m (d) the opposite vector (−106 over 61.0), bearing 300°. Vector components (A1 A1); magnitude / direction (M1 A1); interpretation or generalisation (B/D: R1).

items.stem: Which term matches this description: "Vectors that are scalar multiples of each other: u = kv"?
items.answer: parallel vectors

items.stem: Briefly explain why vector addition is commutative.
items.answer: Adding components is ordinary addition of numbers, which is commutative; geometrically both orders complete the same parallelogram.

items.stem: Explain how you can tell that (−5 over −2) and (−15 over −6) are parallel.
items.answer: The second is 3 times the first (each component), so it has the same line of action.
items.markingKey: Scalar multiple (R1); direction comment (A1).

items.stem: A boat near Singapore moves through the water with velocity (5 over 7) km/h (east, north) and the current is (−1 over 4) km/h. (a) Find the resultant velocity. (b) Find the resultant speed. (c) Find the bearing of the boat’s actual course. (d) Find its displacement after 2 hours.
items.answer: (a) (4 over 11) km/h (b) 11.7 km/h (c) 020° (d) after 2 h: (8 over 22) km from the start

items.stem: Two ropes pull a crate in a warehouse in Mombasa with forces (7 over 6) N and (−6 over 8) N. (a) Find the resultant force. (b) Find its magnitude. (c) Find the third force that would keep the crate still. (d) Explain your answer to (c).
items.answer: (a) (1 over 14) N (b) 14.0 N (c) (−1 over −14) N (d) the three forces then add to the zero vector, so the object is in equilibrium
items.markingKey: (a) (1 over 14) N (b) 14.0 N (c) (−1 over −14) N (d) the three forces then add to the zero vector, so the object is in equilibrium. Vector operations correct (M1 A1 A1); magnitude/direction (A1); interpretation (D/B: R1).

items.stem: Tariq says |a + b| = |a| + |b| for a = (−2 over 4) and b = (−4 over 4). Check this and explain the result.
items.answer: |a + b| = |(−6 over 8)| ≈ 10.0, |a| + |b| ≈ 10.1; they are equal only if a and b point the same way – the third side of a triangle is shorter than the other two together.

items.answer: 2a has the same direction as a with twice the length; scalar multiples are always parallel.

items.answer: Only if a and b point in the same direction; otherwise |a + b| < |a| + |b|.

items.stem: A robot in a factory in Oslo moves (6 over −2), then (2 over 6), then (−1 over 5) (metres). (a) Find its total displacement. (b) Find the straight-line distance from the start. (c) Write the vector that returns it to the start. (d) Explain whether the order of the moves matters for (a).
items.answer: (a) (7 over 9) (b) √130 ≈ 11.4 (c) (−7 over −9) (d) the order of the legs does not change the resultant
items.markingKey: (a) (7 over 9) (b) √130 ≈ 11.4 (c) (−7 over −9) (d) the order of the legs does not change the resultant. Vector operations correct (M1 A1 A1); magnitude/direction (A1); interpretation (D/B: R1).

items.stem: OACB is a parallelogram with OA = a = (−5 over −1) and OB = b = (−1 over 0). (a) Find the diagonal OC. (b) Find the diagonal AB. (c) Find the length of each diagonal. (d) Comment on when the diagonals would be equal.
items.answer: (a) OC = a + b = (−6 over −1) (b) AB = b − a = (4 over 1) (c) |OC| = √37, |AB| = √17 (d) the diagonals are equal only if the parallelogram is a rectangle
items.markingKey: (a) OC = a + b = (−6 over −1) (b) AB = b − a = (4 over 1) (c) |OC| = √37, |AB| = √17 (d) the diagonals are equal only if the parallelogram is a rectangle. Vector operations correct (M1 A1 A1); magnitude/direction (A1); interpretation (D/B: R1).

items.answer: collinear

items.stem: Explain why the position vector of the midpoint of AB is ½(a + b).
items.answer: OM = OA + ½AB = a + ½(b − a) = ½a + ½b.
items.markingKey: Route O → A → M (M1); simplification (A1).

items.stem: "AB = a − b." Explain the flaw in this statement.
items.answer: AB = b − a: from A to B.

items.answer: (a) AB = (−3 over 1), DC = (−3 over 1) (b) AB = DC, so ABCD is a parallelogram (c) midpoint of AC = midpoint of BD = (0, 3/2) (d) the diagonals bisect each other

items.stem: A = (8, −7) and B = (−5, −3). P lies on AB with AP : PB = 2 : 3. Find the position vector of P.

items.answer: (a) m = (−5/2 over −1), n = (1/2 over 2) (b) MN = (3 over 3), BC = (6 over 6) (c) MN = ½BC, so MN ∥ BC and half its length (d) in general MN = ½(c − b) = ½BC

items.stem: OA = a, OB = b, OD = 2a and OC = 2b. (a) Find AB in terms of a and b. (b) Find DC. (c) Prove that ABCD (with A, B, C, D in order around O) is a trapezium. (d) Explain when it would be a parallelogram.
items.answer: (a) AB = b − a (b) DC = 2(b − a) (c) DC = 2AB so AB ∥ DC; ABCD is a trapezium with DC 2 times AB (d) the other sides are not parallel unless k = 1

items.answer: Points that lie on one straight line; A, B, C are collinear if AB = k AC for some scalar k

items.stem: Freya finds AB for A(−2, −2) and B(6, 1) as a − b = (−8 over −3). Explain the mistake.

items.stem: Briefly explain why a plane must point slightly into a crosswind to fly in a straight line to its destination.
items.answer: The wind adds a sideways velocity; the plane must have an opposite sideways component so the resultant points at the destination.

items.stem: A yacht near Lima starts at (−5 over 5) km relative to a lighthouse at the origin and sails with velocity (4 over −1) km/h. (a) Write its position at time t.
